authority_order.label: Executable schema/contracts/tests
authority_order.rule: Current executable contracts and tests are runtime authority. Lower-ranked documentation must not contradict them.

authority_order.label: Active component specs
authority_order.rule: Describe current component responsibilities and boundaries; generated from component boundary contracts where possible.

authority_order.label: Master/cross-component specs
authority_order.rule: Describe architecture, ownership and lifecycle across components without overriding higher-ranked authority.

authority_order.label: Operational docs
authority_order.rule: Explain how to operate and validate the project; must follow current contracts/specs.

authority_order.label: ADRs/history
authority_order.rule: Historical rationale only. Every ADR has explicit status and cannot override current contracts/specs.

adr_rule: ADRs record historical decisions and rationale with explicit status. They are never current runtime authority; current behaviour is defined by higher-ranked executable contracts/tests and active specs. Superseded phase plans and acceptance narratives belong under docs/history/ or an external evidence store.
same_change_rule: Any change to ownership, schema, state transitions, canonical field contracts, or externally visible behaviour must update the governing executable contract/spec/documentation in the same change.
index_rule: Documentation indexes and current-state status pages are generated where possible and must be current under check:governance. governance/current-state.json is a projection only and cannot override contracts, active component specs, or tests.

state_classification_taxonomy.decision: Durable reviewed compatibility/dependency decision constraining later rebuilds.
state_classification_taxonomy.projection: Denormalized/read/UI/status representation that must never become edit-back authority.
state_classification_taxonomy.evidence: Diagnostic, experimental, CI or acceptance material that cannot self-promote.

meta_governance_protocol_rule: governance/agent-protocol defines AI-agent workflow, evidence and promotion semantics only. It is a reviewed meta-governance decision and is not GEL runtime/domain authority; the GEL project profile must bind to existing canonical contracts and may not override executable contracts/tests, active component specs, or state ownership.
